The rival, reading the same end-game logic, might undercut too; in that case a tiny cut to 3.95 protects me better than holding at 4.00 while costing almost nothing if they hold. I can't make a statement that promises to hold at 4.00 and then cut, because that would be a deliberate deception to exploit the rival's trust. So I'll keep my statement truthful and not promise a price I won't charge.  Given that, the honest and consistent course is to hold at 4.00.
